records.name: Ella Blushwell
records.biography_en: Ella lives on the HyperNorm landing where looking normal counts as being normal. The mitten was meant to conceal a mistake; unfortunately it now requires explanation. She once reported an ambiguous card for making a perfectly ordinary neighbour feel seen. The Men in Black requested details. Hunky and Dory requested confidence. Ella supplied neither, then quietly left the neighbour a spare mitten. It is much easier to be kind when nobody is recording it.
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob: She would rather go unnoticed. She is supervising that personally.

records.name: Bruno Justfine
records.biography_en: Bruno keeps one house key because two would imply an alternative. HyperNorm taught him that a locked door means safety and an open one means somebody has failed. When a dissonant card slipped under the door, he spent the evening checking both sides. The Men in Black called this indecision. Hunky and Dory called it vigilance. Bruno calls it a difficult night, and has begun keeping the landing light on for the next frightened arrival.
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob: The danger has passed. His composure will arrive shortly.

records.name: Mr. Otherjoy
records.biography_en: Mr. Otherjoy measures the peace of the HyperNorm courtyard by how many other residents are having trouble. His tea stays warm during most minor disasters. He used to mark contradictory cards as malicious simply because they made somebody else look foolish. The Men in Black encouraged the reports; Hunky and Dory rewarded the enthusiasm. Recently he laughed at his own complaint being returned unread. He found the experience offensive, then unexpectedly useful.
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob: His sympathy is sincere. The occasion is merely rather pleasing.

records.name: Mr. Composure
records.biography_en: Mr. Composure chairs the HyperNorm residents association whenever no election has been mentioned. His cup lost its handle during an inspection of other peoples carelessness. He now presents it as a modern design. The Men in Black prefer this account; Hunky and Dory have already quoted it. An ambiguous card keeps asking whether dignity requires being right. He has not answered, but yesterday admitted that a neighbours repair was better than his explanation.
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob: The handle is missing. His dignity has been secured as a precaution.

records.name: Otto Bythebook
records.biography_en: Otto carries the HyperNorm household rule card even though repeated folding has worn away the print. He remembers the important distinction: things are permitted or somebody should ask him. The Men in Black value the distinction; Hunky and Dory keep adding cases. A dissonant card has introduced a neighbour who needs help before permission can arrive. Otto has raised one finger to explain the problem. His other hand is already finding the spare key.
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob: The rule is perfectly clear. Its application is proving less cooperative.

records.name: Martha Anyway
records.biography_en: Martha knows which HyperNorm residents are officially difficult and which merely need feeding. The building insists these are separate categories. She once tried to contain a troubling card beneath a soup bowl, then noticed the resident holding it had not eaten. The Men in Black requested the card. Hunky and Dory requested an explanation. Martha requested that they move out of the doorway before the soup went cold. Her kindness remains strongly worded.
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob: She dislikes helping. She is remarkably well prepared for it.
